# Code Style Details

Lookup material split out of the `code-style` rule. That rule keeps the size and complexity budget
and the headline bans; this file holds the per-symbol naming table, the full type rules including
the single accepted `interface` exception, module / export / comment conventions, the Workers
runtime constraints, and the exact set of machine-enforced lint rules. Read it when you are naming
something new, deciding between `type` and `interface`, adding a barrel or a default export, or
wondering whether a given rule is actually enforced by Oxlint.

## Naming

- Files: kebab-case (`tenant-context.ts`); React component files may be PascalCase (`Button.tsx`),
  following the React ecosystem convention.
- Types / classes / components: PascalCase.
- Functions / variables: camelCase.
- Module-level true constants: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (`const MAX_PAGE_SIZE = 100` in
  `apps/server/worker/v1/shared.ts`); local `const` stays camelCase.
- Booleans: `is` / `has` / `should` / `can` prefix (`isVerified`, `hasMfa`).
- Avoid abbreviations except the universal ones (`id` / `url` / `db` / `jwt` / `api`); no
  single-letter names except loop indices (`i`, `x`).

## Types (prefer `type`, no `any`, no `enum`)

- **No `any`**: use `unknown` plus narrowing (`typeof`, `in`, discriminant fields). For untyped
  third-party code, declare a local `type` or a `declare` block. Oxlint enforces this as an error.
- **No `enum`**: use an `as const` object plus a union:
  ```ts
  const Role = { Admin: 'admin', Member: 'member' } as const
  type Role = (typeof Role)[keyof typeof Role]
  ```
- **Prefer `type` aliases** for objects, unions, and intersections. The one accepted use of
  `interface` is declaration merging, which `type` cannot express: module augmentation such as
  `declare module` blocks (`apps/server/worker/env.d.ts`, `apps/server/src/router.tsx`) and
  augmenting a third-party empty interface (`ColumnMeta` in
  `packages/web-ui/src/components/ui/DataTable.tsx`). Anywhere else, use `type`.
- Public exported functions declare an explicit return type; internal locals may rely on inference.
- Prefer immutability: `readonly` fields, `ReadonlyArray`, `as const` literals.
- Use `satisfies` on boundary data to check a literal against a type while keeping the narrow type.
- `tsconfig.base.json` already runs `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `noUnusedLocals`,
  `noUnusedParameters`, and `verbatimModuleSyntax`. Never loosen these per package.

## Modules and Exports

- **Prefer named exports**; use `default` only where a framework requires it (React route
  components, the Workers entry `export default`, Vite config files).
- No circular dependencies; one file, one responsibility.
- Import order and formatting are owned by Oxfmt/Oxlint -- do not hand-tune them.
- Barrels (`index.ts` re-exports) are for a package's public entry point only. Do not stack barrels
  layer by layer inside a package (it hurts tree-shaking).

## Control Flow and Comments

- Use early returns to eliminate `else` nesting; validate and bail out first (guard clauses).
- Comments explain **why** (trade-offs, non-obvious constraints), not **what** (the code says that).
- Do not write comments, error handling, or compatibility shims for scenarios that do not exist;
  do not add docs to code you did not touch.
- Every TODO carries an owner or an issue link. No bare TODOs.
- `no-console` is an Oxlint error in SPA and SDK code (`console.warn` / `console.error` allowed).
  It is turned off for `apps/server/worker/**` and the kernel packages (`protocol`, `webauthn`,
  `crypto`, `saml`, `db`, `backend`), where structured server-side logging is expected.

## Workers Runtime Constraints

- Prefer web standard APIs (`fetch`, `Request`, `crypto.subtle`, `URL`). Node APIs only in the
  explicit `nodejs_compat` cases (the flag is on in `apps/server/wrangler.jsonc`; see the
  crypto-boundary rule).
- Watch bundle size and cold start: avoid heavy dependencies, and reach for a platform primitive
  before adding a library (see `docs/design/00-overview.md` section 4, "self-built boundary").

## Machine-Enforced Rules (root `vite.config.ts`)

The `lint.rules` block in the root `vite.config.ts` is deliberately small:

| Rule               | Level                              | Notes                                                            |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `no-console`       | error, allows `warn` / `error`     | off for worker and kernel packages via `lint.overrides`           |
| `no-explicit-any`  | error                              | repo-wide                                                        |
| `max-params`       | warn, 4                            | `apps/server` runs a zero-warning budget, so it is fatal there    |

Type-aware linting is off (`lint.options.typeAware: false`, `typeCheck: false`): tsgo crashed and
under-reported on the larger packages, so type correctness is owned by the separate turbo
`typecheck` task running the official `tsc`. That means `no-floating-promises` and every other
type-aware rule is currently inert -- the async discipline in the error-handling rule is enforced by
review and by `tsc`, not by Oxlint. `max-lines`, `max-lines-per-function`, `complexity`, and
`max-depth` are not configured at all.

To change any threshold, edit `lint.rules` in the root `vite.config.ts`.
